name: 2.4 Box Plots
_note: In progress -- 6 of a planned 12, not pushed. Every source problem in this section reads a FIGURE, and the two box plot questions the bank already had hand the five-number summary over as text, so 'read a box plot' tested reading a sentence. The four new ones draw the plot in SVG. Values are multiples of ten so every number a student reads off lands on a labelled tick. Still to write: what a box plot does and does not tell you about counts, comparing spread across groups, a box plot against a histogram of the same data, and the median-not-centre-of-the-box trap.

questions.title: Read a Box Plot - Take the median and the quartiles off a drawn box plot, compute the interquartile range, and identify which quarter of the data is the most spread out

Outlier Check from a Box Plot - Take the quartiles off a drawn box plot, build the 1.5 times IQR fences from them, decide whether a newly measured value is an outlier, and separate a long whisker from an outlier
Compare Three Box Plots - Read three box plots on a shared axis to find the largest median, find one group's IQR, and say what comparing medians does and does not tell you
Box Plot from a Frequency Table - Read the minimum, first quartile, median and third quartile off a frequency table so the finished box plot can be checked against them
Boxplot - IQR, Fences, and Outlier Check (Context) - From a five-number summary in context, compute IQR and the 1.5*IQR fences, then decide whether a new observation is an outlier

Five-Number Summary from an Unsorted Data Set - Sort a set of readings recorded out of order, find the two quartiles and the median, and compute the interquartile range that spans the middle half of the data
